title: US Debt Hits Record $40 Trillion
paragraphs: The national debt of the United States has passed $40 trillion for the first time, reaching another record and adding to concerns about the country's long-term finances.

The milestone was reached on August 19, according to data from the US Treasury. It came just five months after the debt passed $39 trillion in March, highlighting how quickly the government is borrowing.

The national debt is the total amount of money that the federal government owes, built up over many years in which it has spent more than it has collected in taxes. According to an analysis of Treasury data by Al Jazeera, the current total works out to about $117,000 for every person in the country, or about $297,000 per household.

Several different factors are driving the debt even higher. These include spending on defense, as well as on Social Security and Medicare, the government programs that provide pensions and health care for older Americans. As the population ages, the cost of these programs is rising.

Interest is another major and growing cost. As the debt gets bigger, the government must pay more interest on the money it borrows. The government now spends roughly $1.1 trillion a year on interest payments alone.

Recent laws are also expected to add to the problem. According to the Congressional Budget Office, President Donald Trump's tax and spending law, known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, is projected to add another $4.7 trillion to the debt.

The rising debt may soon create a political challenge. The US has a legal limit on how much the government can borrow, currently set at $41.1 trillion. The Bipartisan Policy Center, a think tank, expects that this limit could be reached sometime between late winter and mid-summer 2027, which would force Congress to act.

Reactions to the new milestone were mixed. A White House spokesman said the administration was focused on cutting waste and growing the economy. However, organizations such as the Peter G. Peterson Foundation, which focuses on government finances, warned that the country's current path is unsustainable.
